official.title: Monthly Climate Assessment and Outlook
official.english_core_text: El Niño increases the likelihood of below-normal rainfall conditions, which may result in adverse impacts such as dry spells and droughts in some areas of the country. Further, based on the said rainfall assessment, nineteen (19) provinces experienced meteorological drought; twenty-nine (29) provinces were under dry spells, and four (4) provinces experienced dry conditions. The ranges of forecast temperature are as follows: 14.6°C – 28.7°C in the mountainous areas of Luzon, 20.2°C – 40.4°C over the rest of Luzon, 21.0°C – 37.8°C in Visayas, 15.4°C – 33.4°C in the mountainous areas of Mindanao, 20.4°C – 38.3°C over the rest of Mindanao, and 23.1°C – 38.0°C for Metro Manila. The rainfall assessment for the month showed that below-to-way-below-normal rainfall conditions were experienced across Luzon and most parts of Visayas, except in the provinces of Bohol, Eastern Samar, Leyte and Southern Leyte, which received near- normal rainfall.

official.title: Seasonal Climate Outlook
official.english_core_text: The rainfall forecast for the JFM season is predicted to be near- to above-normal over most parts of the country, aside from below-normal rainfall conditions over some areas in western Luzon. Central, Quezon City, Metro Manila, Philippines 1100 Website: http://bagong.pagasa.dost.gov.ph Forecast rainfall for this season suggests generally near-normal conditions over most parts of the country, aside from below-normal conditions in some areas of the Ilocos region and the western portions of Central Luzon and CALABARZON. Likewise, the probabilistic forecast indicates a moderate to high chance of above- normal rainfall conditions in most areas of the country. April to June (AMJ) 2026 Outlook Transition from La Niña to ENSO-neutral conditions is anticipated during the season.
